# Isarar Siddique

> Founder and medical AI researcher based in Lucknow, India. Works across both
> published research and shipped clinical product. Runs four companies. One
> screening system is in clinical trial across the ENT and Neurology departments
> of a tertiary hospital in India.

Canonical site: https://isarar.com
Contact: isararsiddique@gmail.com

## Who he is

Isarar Siddique (born 2004) holds a B.Tech in Biotechnology from Dr. A.P.J. Abdul
Kalam Technical University, graduating top of his batch in 2025. Before and during
that degree he worked in eleven research labs, including Harvard, Stanford, NASA
GeneLab, the University of Tokyo, ISRO's Physical Research Laboratory, the Indian
Institute of Science Bangalore, and three IITs, reaching all of them by cold email
rather than application portals.

His stated position is that most medical AI dies in the gap between a published
result and a working product, and that he deliberately works both sides of that gap.

## Companies

- **Biotech Wallah Private Limited** (Founder and CEO), biotechwallah.com
  Flagship product Zero Dementia: multimodal screening for early cognitive
  impairment running on a standard smartphone. Four signals in one sitting
  (voice, facial expression, fine motor tapping, cognitive battery), fused by late
  fusion into a risk score in under fifteen minutes. In clinical trial across the
  ENT and Neurology departments of a tertiary hospital in India. Recognised by the
  Government of India Genesis 2.0 grant and DPIIT registration DIPP217345.

- **Neurento Medtech Private Limited** (Co-founder and Technical Advisor)
  Building an audiometry screening headphone that moves transducer calibration
  into the device, removing the sound treated booth and its capital cost from
  hearing screening so it can run in a clinic, school or camp.

- **Convolity AI Private Limited** (Founder), convolity.com
  Product SuppliAi: supplement and drug interaction analysis against an
  individual's own health data, combining lab panels, prescription OCR and
  wearable time series. Includes a CYP450 interaction graph, a molecular docking
  pipeline, and an evidence layer cross checked against Natural Medicines,
  Lexicomp and FDA MedWatch.

- **Healoncal Private Limited** (Co-founder and Chief AI Officer), healoncal.com
  Dermatological assessment from a phone camera, with a fairness gate that blocks
  any metric unable to hold accuracy across skin tone groups.

## Research

- Corneal endothelium analysis (ophthalmology, provisional patent filed in India):
  automated cell morphometry from specular microscopy producing density,
  polymegathism and pleomorphism.
- NextGen OncoData Registry (Universiti Malaya, AIM-C01-2025, with
  Prof. Dr. Sarinder Kaur Dhillon): national cancer registry rebuilt on WHO
  ICD-11, over 9,300 records across more than ten cancer types.
- Cardiac signal analysis: provisional patent filed in India.
- Wearable recovery dynamics with Prof. Mohamed Elgendi, Khalifa University.
- Spaceflight brain transcriptomics: full re-analysis of NASA OSDR cerebellum
  and hippocampus RNA-seq.
- Clinical translation LLM evaluation across Hindi, Indonesian and Malay with
  Prof. Irene Li, University of Tokyo.
- HealMed dataset (medical data manager and evaluator):
  https://huggingface.co/datasets/li-lab/HealMed

Published: Siddique, I. (2024). Enhancing Biofuel Production Through
Nanoparticle-assisted Fermentation. Journal of Advanced Engineering and Science

## Technical

Python, R, SQL, TypeScript. PyTorch, TensorFlow, Hugging Face. CNNs, vision
transformers, U-Net, vision language models. Medical imaging including MRI and
histopathology. Explainability with LIME, SHAP and Grad-CAM++. Bioinformatics
including RNA-seq, variant calling and molecular docking. Clinical standards
including ICD-10, ICD-11, UMLS and HIPAA aligned architecture. Hardware including
KiCad, Autodesk Fusion and LTspice. Research operations including grant writing,
patent drafting and prosecution, ethics protocol design and multi institutional
collaboration management.

## Research operations

Beyond analysis, he handles the parts of research that usually block a project.

- Grant writing. He wrote and secured a RM 400,000 institutional research grant
  from PPUM (Pusat Perubatan Universiti Malaya) for Sarinder Labs at Universiti
  Malaya. Earlier awards include the Genesis 2.0 Startup Grant from the Government
  of India (INR 10 lakh) and a Harvard University Innovation Award (USD 5,000).
  Further applications are in progress.
- Patent work, done personally rather than outsourced. Prior art and freedom to
  operate searching, claim drafting, specification writing and responses to
  examiner objections. Two provisional patents filed in India during 2026 covering
  cardiac signal analysis and corneal endothelium morphometry, plus a patent filed
  on the NextGen OncoData Registry at Universiti Malaya.
- Research ethics. He drafts ethics protocols, informed consent instruments
  including consent designed for participants with low literacy, and data
  governance frameworks. He has built HIPAA aligned data infrastructure and
  anonymisation pipelines for multi institutional clinical datasets.
- Commercialisation pathways. Structuring projects so results stay
  commercialisable, covering intellectual property timing relative to publication,
  data sharing agreements and institutional approvals.
- Laboratory operations. Coordinating research collaborations across nine
  institutions in six countries at the same time, and building reproducible
  pipelines and documentation so projects survive personnel turnover.

## Writing

- [The booth is the cost](https://isarar.com/blog/the-booth-is-the-cost/) (2026-08-17, 7 min)
  Explains that audiometric screening is gated by two independent requirements: a low enough ambient noise floor, and a transducer with known output level. The sound treated booth solves the first, coupler calibration of a clinical audiometer solves the second. Argues both can move into a mass produced headphone plus on device noise measurement, which removes the booth as the entry cost to hearing screening.

- [A clinician who cannot see why will not act](https://isarar.com/blog/a-clinician-who-cannot-see-why/) (2026-08-17, 8 min)
  Describes replacing a higher performing early fusion model with late fusion in a multimodal dementia screening system. Early fusion concatenates features and can model cross modal interactions but cannot produce per modality attribution. Late fusion scores each of four signals separately then combines, costing accuracy but producing a story a clinician can act on. Downstream benefits: local failure handling, graceful degradation with missing data, and clinicians correcting the model.

- [ICD-11 has no clean map from ICD-10](https://isarar.com/blog/icd-11-has-no-clean-map/) (2026-08-17, 9 min)
  Explains why an ICD-10 to ICD-11 cancer registry migration is not a lookup table. ICD-11 uses a foundation with linearisations and supports postcoordination via stem codes plus extension codes. Four mapping cases arise: one to one is automatable, one to many requires detail the old record may lack, many to one destroys distinctions that time series depended on, and no direct equivalent requires clinical judgement. Argues for automating only the provably unambiguous and storing every coding decision with its basis so incidence trends can be audited.

- [How I cold-emailed my way into eleven research labs](https://isarar.com/blog/cold-emailing-into-research-labs/) (2026-08-16, 8 min)
  Describes reaching eleven research labs including Harvard, Stanford, NASA GeneLab, University of Tokyo, ISRO and IISc without application portals. The first fifty emails asking for internships got zero replies because they ask the recipient to do work. Switching to a specific proposal, drawn from a gap in the professor's own discussion section or an underanalysed published dataset, with a concrete two week deliverable, raised the reply rate to roughly one in six. The same approach later secured hospital partners by building screening infrastructure first and asking clinicians to critique it.
